meeting_header:
Date: 2026-09-15 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 42 minutes
Location: Zoom - Redwood POC
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Sofia Iqbal (Redwood CSM); Liam Ortega (BlueCarbon Lead ML), Priya Nair (BlueCarbon Platform), Grace Huang (BlueCarbon SRE)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review TTFT/streaming buffer experiments and kernel selection tradeoffs. Discussed anomalous spike at long sequence tails, streaming chunk sizing, interaction with KV cache segmentation, and enterprise constraints (VPC/private). Agreed on actions to rerun focused A/B benchmarks and to share representative prompt distributions.
topics: TTFT numbers & variance, streaming buffer sizing, kernel choices and quantization impact, sequence length tail behavior, private deployment implications
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have about forty two minutes on the calendar. quick roll call?
[00:06] Liam: Liam here, Priya, Grace on my end. 
[00:09] Priya: yep, Priya. 
[00:11] Ethan: Ethan from Redwood, hi all. 
[00:14] Sofia: Sofia here. 
[00:17] Maya: awesome. quick agenda: we want to go over the TTFT runs from last week, the streaming buffer experiment, then kernel selection notes and next steps. any blockers?
[00:28] Liam: none on my side, just curious about the big variance we saw last Friday - we saw median TTFT ~110ms but 95th was 520ms which seems ... odd.
[00:40] Ethan: yeah, we dug into that - initial hypothesis is the long sequence tail plus our default streaming chunk size causing extra micro-batching on the runtime, and then KV cache refills take longer. sometimes the transcriber says "K V" as in "K V" which is fine.
[00:59] Priya: when you say chunk size, you mean the streaming write buffer? like how many tokens we flush upstream?
[01:06] Ethan: exactly. by default we flush every 16 tokens for that model at the current quant. but at sequences >800 tokens we started to see backpressure. the runtime will occasionally collapse small batches into a bigger work item and that increases first token latency.
[01:20] Grace: to be clear, our live payloads have a long tail - about 8% over 1k tokens. most synthetic tests were 256-512 so we missed that. we'll send the histogram.
[01:32] Maya: great, makes sense. quick walk through of the runs: last week Redwood ran two kernels - Kernel A (optimized attention tiling) and Kernel B (chunked matmul path). A had slightly better median but B had more stable 95th in our synthetic bench. Ethan?
[01:46] Ethan: mhm. Kernel A median TTFT 108ms, 95th 330ms. Kernel B median 125ms, 95th 270ms. but when we replayed BlueCarbon's long-tail prompts Kernel A 95th jumped to 520ms. we think A's attention tiling performance regresses when sequence length variability increases because of memory remapping on some GPUs.
[02:10] Liam: that matches what we saw in our internal profilers - some GPU memcpy spikes. are these NV* driver things?
[02:16] Ethan: could be driver, could be kernel memory layout. we didn't fully repro on our infra; need your real traffic to repro reliably.
[02:24] Priya: we'll share traffic hist by tomorrow. question on streaming buffer strategy - could we tune to flush earlier to reduce TTFT at the cost of a few more tokens?
[02:35] Maya: yes that's the tradeoff. smaller buffer -> earlier first token but less batching efficiency -> higher token cost. Redwood Optimize can approximate unit-cost delta.
[02:44] Sofia: plus there's effect on throughput SLOs, if we reduce batch size we might need more capacity.
[02:50] Grace: on private deployments, we want deterministic worst-case latency. can Redwood ensure fixed flushe pattern?
[02:57] Ethan: we can pin streaming flush to time thresholds (e.g., 40ms) rather than token counts; that reduces variability. but still, underlying kernel memory behavior matters for 95th.
[03:08] Liam: can you re-run with time-based flush vs token-based?
[03:11] Ethan: yes, we added a time-based flush run in the queue. initial numbers: time-based flush (40ms) median 118ms, 95th 290ms on synthetic; on your long-tail it looks like median 130ms, 95th 300ms. better than token-based A.
[03:28] Priya: curious about KV cache segmentation - Ethan mentioned 64 vs 128 segments earlier, what's the practical impact?
[03:34] Ethan: segmentation affects concurrent access patterns - more segments reduces lock contention on the cache but increases metadata overhead. with a lot of small streams (many users each short), 128 segments helped. with single long sessions segmentation didn't matter as much. in the long-tails we saw some thrash due to segments being rebalanced which bumped the 95th.
[03:52] Grace: so is that a kernel-level choice or runtime config?
[03:55] Ethan: runtime config mainly, but some kernels optimize for specific cache layouts. so the A kernel expects contiguous KV and benefits less from high segmentation. B is more tolerant.
[04:06] Liam: what about quantization? we're using int8 FP16 hybrid per notebook. does that influence TTFT?
[04:12] Ethan: yes, quantization reduces compute time but increases memory pressure sometimes - particularly with int4 backends we saw slower start-up because packing/unpacking on the critical path. int8 hybrid was the sweet spot for these kernels.
[04:26] Priya: ok. on the last run there was a mention of "early token streaming" or "first token fast path" - is that the same as TTFT tuning?
[04:34] Maya: yes, TTFT here means time-to-first-token - we want the first byte to arrive faster for perceived responsiveness. streaming buffer and kernel choices both affect it.
[04:42] Ethan: quick note, our streaming changes introduce some noise in billing - we'll estimate cost delta after we pick a setting.
[04:49] Liam: that's fine if you show the delta. we care more about 95th at this point. if we can get 95th under 350ms we're happy.
[04:56] Maya: noted. objective: get 95th < 350ms on real traffic without >15% unit-cost increase.
[05:03] Priya: small question - did you try adaptive flush (start token-based, then switch to time-based at longer seq)?
[05:09] Ethan: we did a simple adaptive rule in one run: up to 64 tokens token-based, beyond that 40ms time-based. it performed well in synthetic - median 112ms 95th 280ms - but on your long-tail it still had outliers.
[05:24] Grace: the outliers were at the 2k+ sequences?
[05:28] Ethan: yes beyond ~1.6k we see memory remap spikes in kernel A which cause 400-700ms blips depending on GPU.
[05:37] Maya: would a different kernel help for those extreme tails?
[05:40] Ethan: Kernel B was more stable at tails but slightly worse median. Kernel C (experimental fused attention) we can try but it's not stable across all GPU choices and may be slower for mid-length.
[05:52] Liam: can you run A vs B vs C on our tail subset only? that would be helpful.
[05:56] Ethan: yes we can run targeted tails. we'll need your sample prompts and the sequence-length histogram to slice properly.
[06:03] Priya: will provide that. also asked about private deployment - we might do an air-gapped eval where we test kernel C on our appliance, how does Redwood handle kernel licensing there?
[06:14] Maya: for Private we provide the runtime and kernel binaries under the enterprise license; we can coordinate with your procurement. we'll include kernel matrix in the security pack.
[06:24] Grace: any SOC2/ISO items impacted by streaming buffer changes?
[06:28] Sofia: not directly. streaming buffer is runtime behavior. retention, logs, and SSO are unchanged. but we'll note that streaming increases ephemeral in-memory buffers - not persisted.
[06:38] Liam: good. a separate topic - we saw some garbled tokens in long outputs, sometimes "KV" came out as "K V" in transcripts and that confuses our downstream parser. is that Redwood or our ASR?
[06:48] Ethan: likely downstream tokenizer alignment. when we chunk streaming mid-token boundary it can add spaces; we have logic to avoid splitting inside encoded tokens but it depends on tokenizer. we can run a transcript alignment test.
[07:00] Priya: let's do that.
[07:02] Maya: recap of experiments to run: 1) Kernel A vs B vs C targeted on tail subset; 2) Time-based vs token-based vs adaptive flush A/B; 3) KV segmentation 64 vs 128; 4) quantization int8 vs int4 run for median/95th delta. Ethan you'll own the kernel and KV runs. Priya will share hist and prompts.
[07:20] Ethan: yes. i'll script replays and upload the CSVs and flamegraphs. planning 3 runs each, 5-repetition median.
[07:27] Grace: once you share flamegraphs we'll triage with our perf team.
[07:30] Maya: timing - we'll aim to have results by Friday 2026-09-18. does that work?
[07:36] Liam: works. 
[07:38] Priya: yes.
[07:39] Maya: any blockers from Redwood side?
[07:42] Ethan: only if we need on-prem appliance tests for kernel C - that'll need coordination for the binary packaging.
[07:50] Liam: we can host a short access window. procurement might need an MSA but that's separate.
[07:55] Maya: ok. quick Q&A: Grace?
[07:58] Grace: timeline for cost delta estimate?
[08:00] Maya: i'll send a short note with estimated % token-cost change based on the run medians by 2026-09-16.
[08:06] Priya: any chance to test an extreme flush config - flush every 8 tokens - just to see TTFT floor?
[08:11] Ethan: yeah we have a "low-latency mode" run that flushes at 8 tokens; it got median 95ms but unit-cost went up ~28% on synthetic. we'll include that as a reference.
[08:24] Liam: that helps set tradeoffs.
[08:26] Maya: final recap and next steps: (1) BlueCarbon -> send sequence histogram + sample prompts (Priya) by 9/17; (2) Redwood -> run kernel A/B/C on tail subset + KV segmentation runs + adaptive flush experiments, push CSVs and flamegraphs by 9/18 (Ethan); (3) Maya -> cost delta note by 9/16; (4) Schedule kernel selection review 9/22 (all).
[08:52] Sofia: i'll create the calendar invite for 9/22 and add a short agenda.
[08:57] Liam: thanks everyone.
[08:59] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up in thread with links to the benchmark artifacts.
[09:03] (recording ends)

Notes: transcription contains occasional tokenizer/ASR artifacts - proper nouns sometimes misrendered. references made to internal kernel labels (A/B/C) and to streaming/prefix/KV cache behavior. Links referenced: "benchmark CSV" (will be shared in Redwood drive), "flamegraphs" (link to S3).
final_recap: Owners: Ethan to run kernels & KV runs; Priya to share hist+prompts; Maya to send cost note. Target dates 2026-09-16 through 2026-09-18. Follow-up meeting 2026-09-22 for kernel selection review.
